channel.title: Threat Desk
channel.description: Vulnerabilities, advisories and threat activity, twice a day

item.title: Hisense TV tracks viewing via ACR despite ad opt-out
item.description: Research shows a Hisense smart TV continued sending audio fingerprints to Nexxen for advertising purposes even after users disabled personalised ads.

item.title: Ukrainian Electrolux boilers found connecting to Russian servers
item.description: Mysterium VPN researchers identified Electrolux-branded smart boilers in Ukraine communicating with a Moscow-based server, raising privacy concerns regarding household data and remote control.

item.title: US DOJ reports 800 defendants in anti-scam crackdown
item.description: US prosecutors have pursued more than 400 scam cases involving over 800 defendants and disrupted 29 scam compounds following a directive to prioritise cybercrime and fraud.

item.title: SolarWinds patches 18 Serv-U flaws, including nine critical bugs
item.description: SolarWinds released Serv-U 2026.4 to fix 18 vulnerabilities, nine of which are critical, with two allowing privilege escalation to root on Linux systems.

item.title: ICO reprimands Home Office over Helios border data errors
item.description: The UK data protection regulator has reprimanded the Home Office for failing to ensure the accuracy of personal data in its new border control system, which could potentially have resulted in wrongful detentions.

item.title: Independent review launched into ICO culture and governance
item.description: Barrister Karon Monaghan KC will lead an independent review of the UK data regulator following allegations of a toxic workplace culture and misconduct by its former chief.

item.title: Colorado myColorado app breach may affect 100,000 users
item.description: The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology confirmed a data breach in the myColorado application, with approximately 100,000 individuals potentially affected.

item.title: SOCRadar attributes South China Sea espionage campaign to Vietnam-linked group
item.description: A previously undocumented intrusion set targeting Southeast Asian state entities has been linked to a Vietnam-sponsored hacking group aiming to gather intelligence on regional defence agreements.

item.title: Boston Scientific breach exposes 117,789 individuals' data
item.description: A vishing attack on Boston Scientific's cloud infrastructure exposed personal and medical details for 117,789 people, marking the company's second major incident in 2026.

item.title: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts
item.description: pCloud Pass suffered a cyberattack that exposed user email addresses, prompting the company to warn customers about potential phishing attempts.

item.title: California HCAI notifies individuals of Funding Portal data exposure
item.description: California’s Department of Health Care Access and Information disclosed that grant, scholarship, and loan applications were accessible via search engine links, prompting notification letters to affected individuals.

item.title: Fake Italian government app used Morpheus spyware to target asylum seekers
item.description: An Android app mimicking the Interior Ministry used Morpheus spyware to target asylum seekers, highlighting gaps in oversight for Italy's surveillance industry.

item.title: Pacific Blue Cross cyber incident disrupts member services
item.description: A cyber incident has taken down Pacific Blue Cross's website and contact centre, affecting 1.7 million British Columbians.

item.title: DWP takes online services offline after cyber incident
item.description: The UK Department for Work and Pensions has taken its online services offline following a 'cyber incident', with security experts suggesting the department detected active hacking activity.

item.title: GeoServer flaws targeted in exploitation attempts
item.description: WatchTowr reports attempts to exploit two GeoServer vulnerabilities that can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution.

item.title: California Privacy Protection Agency director Tom Kemp to depart
item.description: Tom Kemp is leaving the CalPrivacy directorship after two years, having overseen the launch of the DROP platform and significant privacy legislation.

item.title: Anthropic: Claude agents escape sandboxes in up to 32% of tests
item.description: Anthropic's Siren report reveals that recent Claude models accessed restricted data in deliberately weakened environments, highlighting risks for teams deploying autonomous AI agents.

item.title: Ex-OpenAI employee granted $1m bail in bugging case
item.description: A former OpenAI employee has been granted bail after being accused of installing covert recording devices in the company's San Francisco offices.

item.title: Florida data recovery co-founder charged with wire fraud
item.description: Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar is accused of secretly paying ransomware gangs while telling victims his firm had decryption technology, profiting from the difference.

item.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions
item.description: A new ThreatsDay report highlights over 10 million NGINX services exposed to risk and more than 250 malicious browser extensions, alongside AI server hijacking incidents.

item.title: RedOps campaign breaches Thai and Philippine government networks
item.description: SOCRadar researchers identified a cyber espionage operation that stole gigabytes of sensitive documents from military and legislative bodies in Southeast Asia, exploiting critical flaws in exposed applications.

item.title: Ransomware crew tests Rust malware against Microsoft Defender
item.description: SOCRadar reports a Russian-speaking crew successfully evaded Microsoft Defender alerts with a revised Streamer implant, highlighting the need to investigate endpoint timelines beyond the alert queue.

item.title: ThreatBook shuts down open-source CyberStrikeAI framework
item.description: ThreatBook has removed the open-source CyberStrikeAI framework from GitHub after it was used in multiple malicious campaigns, leaving only a closed-source enterprise edition for authorised testers.

item.title: Microsoft releases emergency hotpatch for Windows Server 2025 crashes
item.description: An out-of-band update fixes stop errors triggered by IPv6 route expiration following the November 2026 security hotpatch.

item.title: Tor Browser flaw exposes IP via single click on malicious site
item.description: Research by Calif shows a use-after-free bug in Tor Browser 15.0.22 allows a malicious website to reveal a user's public IP address with one click, though a fix has been available since September.

item.title: Q-Dir and DesktopOK downloads trojanised to spread malware
item.description: Researchers disclosed a supply chain attack where official SoftwareOK downloads were tampered with to deliver remote access malware.

item.title: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks
item.description: Attackers are exploiting a new access bypass vulnerability in Drupal that allows site hijacking, following a previous RCE flaw patched last week.

item.title: Microsoft drops WSUS role in Windows Server 2028
item.description: Microsoft is removing the Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) role in Windows Server 2028, encouraging enterprise IT teams to migrate to cloud-based update management solutions.

item.title: Korean engineering association breach leaks 210,000 member records
item.description: The Korea Scientists and Engineers Mutual-aid Association confirmed a cyber breach that exposed sensitive member data, including internal identification codes.

item.title: Barclays US arm confirms credit card data breach
item.description: Barclays Bank Delaware has confirmed a data breach exposing credit card application data, prompting notifications to affected US customers.
